title: Atomic‐Scale Insights Into the Thermal Stability of High‐Entropy Nanoalloys

recollection.starting_material: Guess: Equimolar five-component high-entropy alloy nanoparticles (fcc) composed of noble metals such as Ag–Au–Cu–Pd–Pt, 3–10 nm in diameter on a carbon/oxide support, prepared by simultaneous wet-chemical co-reduction.
recollection.intervention: Guess: In situ high-temperature aberration-corrected STEM with atomic-resolution Z-contrast and STEM-EDS/EELS mapping during stepwise heating (room temperature to 800–1000 C), complemented by atomistic simulations (lattice Monte Carlo/MD calibrated by DFT segregation/interaction energies) to interpret segregation and ordering.
recollection.structure: Guess: A single-phase random fcc solid solution at room temperature that develops pronounced radial chemical gradients upon heating—surface (shell) enrichment in low–surface-energy elements (Ag, Au) and interior enrichment in higher–melting/strongly bonding elements (Pt, Pd, Cu), evolving into an onion-like core–shell architecture at higher temperatures; small particles maintain more homogeneous mixing to higher temperatures than larger ones.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: Size-dependent competition between configurational entropy (stabilizing mixing), surface-energy-driven segregation (McLean-type surface enrichment of Ag/Au), and bulk pairwise interactions that favor partial demixing; rapid surface/boundary diffusion governs early segregation, while slower lattice diffusion controls deeper compositional reorganization; at elevated T, the reduced entropic benefit in larger particles allows spinodal-like decomposition into core–shell domains; coalescence/Ostwald ripening further accelerates segregation.
recollection.results: Guess: Random fcc mixing sustained up to ~500–600 C for 3–5 nm particles, with detectable surface segregation starting ~300 C (surface Ag+Au rising from ~40 at% to ~70 at% by 500 C; Cu at surface dropping below ~5 at%); above ~700 C, emergence of a Pd/Pt-rich core and Ag/Au-rich shell with radial composition differences exceeding 30–40 at% over ~1–2 nm; smaller particles (<5 nm) delay demixing by ~150–200 C compared to >8 nm particles; interdiffusion activation energies extracted from in situ line-scan kinetics on the order of 0.6–1.0 eV and Arrhenius D at 600 C ~10^-19–10^-18 m^2 s^-1; overall, thermal stability is enhanced by nanoscale entropy but ultimately limited by surface-driven segregation at high temperature.

score.note: The recollection correctly infers in situ heating with atomic-resolution STEM and atomistic simulation, plus surface-energy-driven segregation and reshaping/coalescence-enhanced diffusion. However, it misidentifies the alloy, synthesis, support, detailed structure, segregating species, and thermal-stability interpretation. It incorrectly invokes Ag/Pd, persistent entropy stabilization, and core-shell demixing trends. The reported temperatures, compositions, activation energies, and size effects do not match the key actual quantitative result of 22% size reduction at 973 K.
